SPECIFICATION FOR RIDGER, ANIMAL-DRAWN

( First Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) WAS adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 July 1979, after the draft finalized by the Soil Working Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. Ridger is an implement used to form ridges required for certain rowor row-planted crops in well-tilled soil. The ridger is also used for forming field furrows or channels, earthing up and similar other It is also known by the names ridging plough and ridger operations. plough or double-mouldboard plough. The ridger generally has a Vshaped or wedge-shaped share fitted to the frog. The nose or point of the share penetrates into the soil and breaks the soil. The mouldboards lift, invert and cast aside the soil, forming channels and ridges of the required size.
sown

0.2

0.3 With the progressive adoption of improved agricultural practices, the use of the ridgers have increased. Hence, it was found desirable to lay down a standard for this implement and thereby providing a better quality of this implement. Keeping this in view, this standard was published in Since then, considerable development has been made in the design 1963. (lf'ridgers. A need was, therefore, felt to revise the standard to incorporate latest modifications. 0.4 This standard is related to the manufacturing and the trade practices prevailing in the country. The figures given in the standard arc meant to serve only as illustrations of various terms and should not be considered as suggestive of any standard design. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement ofthis standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, ezpresoff in accordance with sing the result of a test, shall be rounded The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : Z-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. *Rules for rounding
off numerical values ( mired )..

6.1.1 The size shall be declared. The tolerance on declared size shall be f5 mm. 6.2 In case the ridger is provided with sole plate, the vertifical suction for V-shaped share and wedge-shaped share shall be in the range of 3 to 8 mm and 8 to 22 mm respectively. The suction shall be declared by the manufacturer. The suction shall not differ by & 1 mm of the declared value. 6.3 When the ridger is set at its working position, shall be in the range of 250 to 500 mm. the throat clearance

6.4 The ridger shall be provided with one or two handles. If two handles are provided, the distance between the handle grips shall be between 550 and 650 mm. 6.5 When the plough is set at its working position, the vertical distance between the ground and the centre of the grip shall be adjustable. The value shall lie between 800 and 1 100 mm. 6.6 The handle grip shall be circular or oval in cross section. The diameter or minor axis shall be between 25 and 30 mm. The length of the grip shall be not less than 125 mm. The angle between the grip and the handle shall be between 100 to 105". 6.7 The gauge wheel, if provided, shall be not less than 150 mm in diameter and its face width not less than 50 mm. 6.8 The gap between cleavage edge of share and mouldboard shall be not more than 2 mm. 6.9 The cutting edge of the share shall be bevclled to a distance between 5 and 10 mm. The thickness of the cutting edge should be between O-5 to 2 mm. `I'he variation in edge thickness in a share shall be not more than f 0'5 mm. 6.10 The angle of cut for V-shaped share shall be 50 to 80" and for wedge-shaped share shall be 30 to 60". The variation from declared angle shall be not more than + 3". 6.11 The angle of penetration shall be 15 to 30". declared angle shall be not more than f 3". 7. OTHER The variation from

FINISH

8.1 The components of the ridger should be free from pits, burrs, cracks and other visual defects. The castings shall be free from blow holes. Welded joints shall not be porous. 8.2 The surface of the parts of the plough shall shall have a protective coating which will prevent transit and storage. 9. MARKING AND PACKING on non-wearing trade-mark, surface with if any; be evenly dressed and surface deterioration in

9.1 MarkingEach ridger shall be marked the following particulars: a) Manufacturer's b) Size; and c) Batch or code number. 11 name and recognized

IS : 2565 - 1979 9.1.1 The ridger may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark.

- The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the NOTIS Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
